decisions.basis_note: Two inherited Atlas-10 serine-protease entries are candidate examples, while the fingerprint also names esterases, lipases, and cutinases; no family-wide equivalence is asserted.
The label spans phosphatases, amidohydrolases, and beta-lactamases, so a single source mechanism would be under-scoped.
This is a peptidase-focused specialization within the broader metal-hydrolase surface; no representative entry was adjudicated.
The fingerprint narrows metal hydrolysis toward phosphodiesters and nucleic-acid substrates but still mixes several reaction contexts.
The monoester scope is narrower than generic metal hydrolysis, but the seed set includes mechanistically distinct phosphatase families.
The label combines beta-lactam hydrolysis, deamination, and cyclic-amide hydrolysis without an adjudicated shared mechanism object.
M0049 is a source candidate for one PLP decarboxylation context; the fingerprint also spans transfer, racemization, and other PLP chemistries.
M0767 is a non-detailed radical-SAM source candidate, while the fingerprint spans many distinct radical outcomes and cluster contexts.
Inherited Atlas-3 M0062 is a candidate example for an AdoCbl rearrangement; broader substrate and cofactor-state applicability remains unreviewed.
M0132 supplies one source candidate, but the fingerprint aggregates several flavin oxygenation strategies and substrate classes.

M0133 is a heme monooxygenase candidate within a label that also names peroxidases and oxidases; equivalence is explicitly unresolved.
M0133 is a source candidate for P450cam; the fingerprint specializes the broader heme-oxidase bucket but still spans many P450 contexts.
M0129 is a taurine-dioxygenase candidate; transfer to the full Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate space requires applicability review.
The seed set spans multiple acyl-transfer architectures and acceptor types, with no adjudicated common source mechanism.
M0081 is one cofactor-independent rearrangement candidate, but the negative definition by cofactor absence does not specify a coherent mechanism class.
Three source candidates expose distinct electron acceptors, auxiliary cofactors, and reaction directions under the same broad Mo-cofactor label.
M0135 is a copper-dependent monooxygenase candidate, while the fingerprint includes multicopper oxidases and copper amine chemistry.
Inherited Atlas-10 M0187 is a metal-dependent racemase candidate; the fingerprint also names non-metal and macromolecular epimerization contexts.
The label spans multiple ATP activation chemistries and oligomeric architectures, so no single mechanism object is an adequate match.
M0052 is a class-II fructose-bisphosphate aldolase candidate and is deliberately paired with M0222 to retain same-EC mechanistic alternatives.
Inherited Atlas-10 M0216 is a carbonic-anhydrase candidate, while the label aggregates other zinc-dependent lyase and hydratase contexts.
The fingerprint groups multi-component and single-chain biotin carboxylation systems without a reviewed component-state mapping.
This substrate-focused kinase specialization has no adjudicated source entry in the bounded draft.
The family is narrower than a general kinase fingerprint, but no exact source-object equivalence was established during Phase A.
The fingerprint primarily bridges an architecture/fold grouping to multiple reaction labels; it is not itself a reviewed mechanism.
The GHMP grouping is useful for cross-source family lookup but does not select one substrate-specific reaction or mechanism.
This is a reaction- and fold-focused specialization; no direct source handle was frozen in Phase A.
The PfkB/ribokinase family links fold/family annotations to several EC reactions and therefore behaves as a bridge rather than one mechanism.
M0106 and M0219 are distinct ThDP source candidates; their coexistence demonstrates that the cofactor label aggregates multiple transformations.
The cofactor-oriented fingerprint spans many substrates and auxiliary cofactors; two source candidates are lookup examples only.
M0970 is a polymerizing glycosyltransferase candidate, while the fingerprint spans many donors, acceptors, and processivity regimes.
Inherited Atlas-10 M0203 carries alternatives for one glycoside hydrolase; the fingerprint spans retaining, inverting, and substrate-specific contexts.
The fingerprint aggregates transfers to different atoms and macromolecular or small-molecule acceptors; no direct candidate was adjudicated.
Inherited Atlas-3 proves M0138 is Cu/Zn SOD and counterevidence only; no Mn/Fe M-CSA mechanism is transferred into this row.
The label groups ionization-initiated and protonation-initiated cyclizations across distinct substrates without one adjudicated source object.
The fingerprint bridges protein-family/fold annotations to substrate-residue classes and does not by itself fix a protein-specific catalytic state.
The Asp-phosphoenzyme scope is narrower than general phosphatase labels, but no row-level source match was retained in the bounded acquisition.
The fingerprint is substrate-class specific, while phosphorylation-coupled and non-phosphorylating variants make exact equivalence unsafe without review.
This fold/family specialization overlaps the broader Ser-His-Asp/Glu label but does not establish shared substrate applicability or exact steps.
The protein-substrate specialization remains broader than any one PPP, PPM, or calcineurin mechanism and has no adjudicated direct handle.
The bond-type specialization does not resolve substrate, leaving-group, or protonation applicability across the seed families.
The label is defined chiefly by absence of a metal and mixes cyclic-nucleotide and other phosphodiester contexts without a supported common mechanism.
The antibiotic-substrate specialization is plausible as a family lane, but position specificity and family applicability remain unresolved.
Inherited Atlas-3 M0002 is a TEM-1 candidate with an explicit alternative; transfer across serine beta-lactamase classes is not asserted.
The SDR family is narrower than the NAD(P) bucket but still spans distinct substrates and reaction directions without a frozen direct handle.
The AKR family specialization remains reaction- and substrate-ambiguous, and no representative source mechanism was adjudicated.
The family lane is narrower than generic acyl transfer, but acceptor position and acetyltransferase architecture remain applicability gaps.
This metal-dependent beta-lactamase specialization shares an EC label with serine enzymes but must retain its distinct metal chemistry and class variability.
M0851 is a non-detailed glutathione-peroxidase candidate; the fingerprint also names peroxiredoxin families with different resolving chemistry.
The PAPS donor is shared while acceptor type, topology, and substrate scope vary; no exact source mechanism was adjudicated.
The GST label covers many electrophiles, reaction outcomes, and classes, so the machine draft treats it as an aggregation.
Class I, class II, editing, and amino-acid specificity make this a multi-mechanism aggregation rather than one transferable object.
The acid-to-CoA activation lane is narrower than ATP-dependent ligases, but substrate range and domain architecture remain unresolved.
M0174 is a papain candidate, while caspases, calpains, and deubiquitinases make the fingerprint a broader aggregation.
The disulfide-reductase lane narrows the flavin redox bucket but still spans distinct electron donors, relay cysteines, and oligomeric contexts.
The narrow EC/family scope and M0112 make exact duplication a machine-draft candidate classification only; real review can still reject it.
